EAMS / Faculty & research staff
Directory

Faculty & research staff

Thirty-eight scholars across earth sciences, atmospheric chemistry, marine ecology, paleoclimate, and earth-systems modeling. Most teach undergraduate courses every semester and advise PhD students from their own labs.

Listings are organized by faculty rank. Office numbers refer to Mendel Hall; field-station and shared-lab assignments are noted parenthetically. Most office hours are by appointment during the summer.

Professors 11 faculty

Asha Mahalingam

Department Chair · Henry C. Brennan Professor of Physical Oceanography
Physical oceanography · AMOC variability · tracer chemistry

Mahalingam's lab uses tracer chemistry and bottom-mounted moorings to reconstruct overturning circulation in the western North Atlantic over the past 200 years. Recent work focuses on the seasonal cycle of the Labrador Current and its sensitivity to Greenland meltwater pulses.

Theodore Kasprzak

Eleanor Hartwell Professor of Sedimentary Geology
Sedimentology · basin analysis · coastal stratigraphy

Kasprzak studies how shallow-marine sediments record sea-level change on decadal to millennial timescales. His group has logged more than 3,000 m of vibracore from the Gulf of Maine and now operates a permanent stratigraphic monitoring transect across the Cobbett Bay barrier-island system.

Wei-Ling Tan

Professor of Atmospheric Sciences
Synoptic meteorology · heat waves · mid-latitude dynamics

Tan's research focuses on the dynamics of persistent mid-latitude weather regimes — blocking highs, heat domes, and the stalled jet patterns associated with North Atlantic SST anomalies. She maintains the Brennan reanalysis composite catalog and co-runs the department's public-facing forecasting seminar.

Babatunde Adeyemi

Professor of Atmospheric Chemistry
Aerosol–cloud interactions · coastal boundary layer

The Adeyemi group operates a four-station coastal aerosol observatory along the Massachusetts Bay sea-breeze front, combining cavity-ringdown spectroscopy with airborne sampling to characterize secondary organic aerosol from marine sources. Recent NSF support extends the network southward to Buzzards Bay.

Inga Rasmussen

Professor of Paleoclimate
Stable isotopes · lacustrine records · Holocene hydroclimate

Rasmussen reconstructs Holocene hydroclimate from lake sediments in the northeastern US and the Faroe Islands, using carbonate δ18O and biomarker hydrogen isotopes. Her group has produced the longest continuous varve record from a New England lake (8,400 years, Lake Atticut).

Daniel Okonkwo

Professor of Marine Geochemistry
Trace metals · sediment-water interface · estuarine biogeochemistry

Okonkwo investigates how trace metals (Mn, Fe, U) cycle across the sediment-water interface in estuaries undergoing eutrophication recovery. His lab developed the open-source fluxprofile code now used in 40+ estuarine programs worldwide.

Mikhail Petrov

Professor of Geodynamics
Continental tectonics · numerical modeling · lithospheric deformation

Petrov develops finite-element models of slow lithospheric deformation, with applications to passive-margin subsidence and the long-wavelength uplift of the Iberian Peninsula. He directs the department's tectos computational cluster (1,200 cores).

Renata Volponi

Professor of Marine Biology
Benthic invertebrates · bivalve ecology · marine heatwaves

Volponi runs a 22-year time series of intertidal community composition at five rocky-shore stations between Cape Ann and Mount Desert Island. Her lab's work on the 2012 and 2018 marine heatwaves has shaped how regional fisheries managers think about post-disturbance recovery in cold-temperate systems.

Haruki Ito

Professor of Volcanology and Igneous Petrology
Arc volcanism · melt inclusions · eruption forecasting

Ito combines melt-inclusion geochemistry with thermodynamic modeling to understand pre-eruptive volatile behavior in arc systems. His group's work at Sakurajima and Soufrière Hills has been cited in operational forecasting protocols by both JMA and the Montserrat Volcano Observatory.

Hendrik de Boer

Professor of Hydrology
Groundwater · coastal aquifers · saltwater intrusion

de Boer studies coastal aquifer dynamics under combined stress from sea-level rise and groundwater pumping. His group operates a 28-well monitoring network across the Cobbett Bay watershed and has helped four Cape Cod towns redesign their wellfield management plans.

Lucia Marchetti

Professor of Marine Ecology
Plankton dynamics · ocean color · biogeochemical–ecosystem coupling

Marchetti links satellite ocean-color products to in-situ plankton-community measurements in the Gulf of Maine. Her group's algorithm for distinguishing diatom and dinoflagellate blooms from MODIS reflectance is now incorporated into the NOAA Northeast HAB warning system.

Sarah Two-Hawk

Associate Professor of Glaciology
Ice-sheet dynamics · Greenland outlet glaciers · firn modeling

Two-Hawk combines GPS and InSAR observations with thermomechanical ice-flow models to study the response of Greenland's outlet glaciers to subglacial hydrology. Her group has run three field seasons at Helheim and Kangerlussuaq.

Priya Singh

Associate Professor of Marine Microbiology
Microbial biogeochemistry · nitrogen cycling · oxygen-minimum zones

Singh studies the microbial communities that drive nitrogen loss from oxygen-minimum zones, with field programs in the eastern tropical North Pacific and the Arabian Sea. Her lab specializes in stable-isotope tracer techniques for measuring anammox and denitrification rates at sea.

Jensen's group quantifies how reactive nitrogen species evolve along rural-to-urban transects in the northeast US, combining tower observations, mobile sampling, and a long-running precipitation chemistry record at the Cobbett Point station.

Associate Professor of Structural Geology

Pawel Kowalczyk

Associate Professor of Paleobiology
Marine paleoecology · Cenozoic mollusks · mass-extinction recovery

Kowalczyk studies the ecological assembly of marine communities after the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction, using assemblage-level statistics on Cenozoic mollusk faunas. He runs the department's paleontology teaching collection (over 32,000 specimens).

Sofia Arroyo

Associate Professor of Coastal Engineering & Geomorphology
Salt marshes · coastal sediment transport · nature-based defenses

Arroyo's group studies how New England salt marshes maintain elevation under accelerating sea-level rise, with paired field-monitoring and numerical modeling at three reference sites. Her work informs both Massachusetts CZM policy and the Town of Brennan's shoreline management plan.

Ezra Okonkwo-Lin

Associate Professor of Physical Oceanography
Mesoscale dynamics · satellite altimetry · Gulf Stream variability

Okonkwo-Lin combines satellite altimetry and Argo float profiles to quantify mesoscale eddy heat transport along the Gulf Stream extension. He teaches the department's introductory oceanography sequence and is on sabbatical at IFREMER in 2026–27.

Harold Thurston

Professor Emeritus of Marine Geology
